### The deprecated import route

`POST .../oauth/import-tokens` still works, and is removed 90 days after th
e\naccounts API shipped. It uploads to your default account, creating an unnamed\none when the server has none, and keeps its old
body and its old\n`{ imported, expiresAt }` answer. Every answer carries `Deprecation: true`, a\n`Sunset` date and a `Link` to `..

./accounts`.

An account this route creates is hosted-only. An existing default it writes
into keeps whatever rule it had. Its
`serverUrl` must be the URL saved in the\nproject, or the answer is `400`. `authorizationServerUrl`, `oauthResourceUrl`\nand `toke

ns.id_token` are accepted and ignored. Move to
`PUT .../accounts/{account}`, which names the account it writes.

The error code
s these routes add to `details.code` are listed in the\n[error code reference](https://docs.mcpjam.com/troubleshooting/error-codes

.md#server-account-errors).

## Run evals from the API

The shortest useful loop: create a run with one inline test, then poll

:

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
# 1. Create (responds 202 immediately; -f + jq -e fail fast on errors)
RUN_ID=$
(curl -fsS -X POST \\\n \"https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/eval-runs\" \\\n -H \"Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM
_API_KEY\" \\\n -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n -d '{\n \"suiteName\": \"smoke\",\n \"serverIds\": [\"'$SERVER_

ID'"],
 "tests": [{
 "title": "echo works",
 "runs": 1,
 "model": "anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5",

"provider": "anthropic",
 "steps": [
 { "id": "s1", "kind": "prompt", "prompt": "Use the ec
\"type\": \"toolCalledWith\",\n \"toolName\": \"echo\",\n \"args\": { \"args\": { \"text\": \"hi\" } }\
d_out\ncurl -s \"https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/eval-runs/$RUN_ID\" \\\n -H \"Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_A

PI_KEY"

# 3. If it did not pass, read the decision summary FIRST
curl -s "https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID
/eval-runs/$RUN_ID/decision-summary\" \\\n -H \"Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY\"\n\n# 4. Or go straight to per-iteration t
ool calls, token usage, latency\ncurl -s \"https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/eval-runs/$RUN_ID/iterations\" \\\n

-H "Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY"
```

The decision summary composes steps 2 and 4 into one versioned object so eve

ry
client reads a run the same way. Four things to know before gating on it:

* **`measurementUnit` ships with every count.** U
nder per-case grading the\n counts are case-execution *variants*, with iterations as trials inside them;\n under a suite-wide ac
curacy threshold they are trials. The same suite reports\n a different total under each, 3 against 15 for three cases run five ti

mes,
 so a count without its unit is not a fact, and a rate is never converted
 across that line.
* **It explains the verdict
; it never re-decides it.** The run's own decision is\n the authority and is carried through on `decision`. The per-trial\n `dia
gnostics` sit underneath it. A case can pass with a failing trial in it,\n so tallying diagnostics gives a different answer than
the platform reached.\n* **`verdict: \"notEstablished\"` is not a failure and not `inconclusive`.** It\n means no verdict exists
at all (unfinished, stopped early, or undecidable);\n `undecided.reason` says which. `inconclusive` *is* a decision; the validity

phase ran and withheld a verdict.
* **`diagnostics.complete` says whether you have the whole list.** A page
 fetched with a

`cursor` is never complete, and `scannedIterations` separates
 "nothing failed" from "we did not look".

Evidence is scop
ed to the claim it supports: for a measured failure the span\nids, prompt indexes and reasons come from the first failed stage's r

ow alone,
and `evidence.tracePath` is an API-relative path you can append to your base URL
to read the full trace.

`model` ta
kes an id from the hosted catalog (`provider/name` form, e.g.\n`anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5`) and runs on your organization's credi
ts.\nProvider-native ids (e.g. `claude-sonnet-4-5`) are bring-your-own-key: pass\nthe key in `modelApiKeys`. A model the API can't
execute is rejected at\ncreate time with `VALIDATION_ERROR`; `details.hostedModels` lists the valid\nhosted ids for that provider

.

Reruns are even shorter: `{ "suiteId": "..." }` reruns the suite exactly as
configured, connecting the suite's saved ser
ver selection (the `202` response\nlists the resolved `servers`). Pass `serverIds` to override the selection; a\nsuite with no sav

ed selection requires it (`VALIDATION_ERROR` with
`details.reason: "NO_SAVED_SERVER_SELECTION"` otherwise).

### Running agai

nst a project environment

A [project environment](#endpoints) is launchable only through a suite that has
it **attached**. Att
ach them first with\n`PATCH /projects/{projectId}/eval-suites/{suiteId}` and an `environmentIds`\narray (send `null` to detach the
m all; `[]` is rejected, use `null`), then\npass `environmentId` on the run. It must be one of that suite's attached\nenvironments
; anything else is a `400` with\n`details.reason: \"ENVIRONMENT_NOT_ATTACHED\"`, raised before any case is\nauthored or any server

connected.

Omitting `environmentId` is meaningful, and depends on the suite:

* **no** attached environments → the run uses
the saved server selection, as before;\n* **exactly one** attached → that environment is used automatically. The `202`\n response
's `environment` field says so;\n* **several** attached → `400` with `details.reason: \"ENVIRONMENT_REQUIRED\"`,\n naming the can

didates.

The environment supplies the closed server set, so `serverIds` is not required and is
**rejected** alongside it (`400
`), rather than accepted and ignored: honoring\nboth would connect a different set than the run is stamped with. The same goes\nfo

r a `serverIds` override on an environment-based suite
(`details.reason: "ENVIRONMENT_SERVERS_NOT_OVERRIDABLE"`).

The run is
pinned to the environment revision resolved at launch: if the\nenvironment changes in between, the run is rejected with `CONFLICT

` (409)
rather than executing against a different configuration than the one whose
tools were captured. Use
`GET /projects/{pro

jectId}/environments/{environmentId}/resolve` to see what it
will connect before launching.

When creating a new inline suite,
`POST .../eval-runs` also accepts `hosts: [{ host: \"Claude\", servers: [\"my-server\"] }]`, using the same host name or ID and op
tional server selection as `POST .../eval-suites`. A single host is selected for the run automatically. With multiple attachments,
use `namedHostId` to select the run's client. For an existing suite, update its attachments first. If `hosts` is omitted, the run
uses the project's default client.\n\nRun reads and listings expose `client: { id, name, source, hostStyle?, modelId? }` when rec
orded. `id` is the named host ID or `null`; `source` is `environment`, `attached_host`, `suite_default`, or `sdk`. The name is dur
able even if the host is deleted. SDK executions use `SDK harness`; `launcher.client` separately identifies the launching process.
Older runs without a descriptor omit `client`. `modelSource: \"case\"` means the run's sole model came from its case snapshot; `c
lient_default` and `override` retain their existing meanings.\n\nEvery run records which environment it used. `GET .../eval-runs/{
runId}` (and\nthe run listings) return `environment: { id, name, revision }` (read from the\nrun's immutable snapshot, not the sui

te's current attachments) or `null` for a
run that used a saved server selection.

Per-organization
concurrency is capped (def
ault **2** concurrent runs); exceeding it returns\n`429` with `details.reason: \"CONCURRENT_RUN_LIMIT\"`; wait for an active run\n

to finish.

If a server answers `401 OAUTH_REQUIRED`, complete the OAuth flow yourself
(the SDK's `runOAuthLogin` handles inter
active, headless, and\nclient-credentials flows) and upload the token to one of the server's\n[accounts](#server-accounts). Subseq
